---- MODULE W4Od12m3p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Units == {"u1", "u2"}
Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
Hospitals == {"h1", "h2"}
NONE == "none"
MaxEpoch == 3

VARIABLES leader, epoch, alloc, pool, grants

vars == <<leader, epoch, alloc, pool, grants>>

Reqs == [unit : Units, hosp : Hospitals]

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ alloc = [u \in Units |-> NONE]
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ grants = {}

Elect(n) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, pool, grants>>

Fail(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, pool, grants>>

Request(u, h) ==
    /\ [unit |-> u, hosp |-> h] \notin pool
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {[unit |-> u, hosp |-> h]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, alloc, grants>>

Serve(m) ==
    /\ leader # NONE
    /\ m \in pool
    /\ alloc[m.unit] = NONE
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![m.unit] = m.hosp]
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {[unit |-> m.unit, hosp |-> m.hosp]}
    /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch>>

Idle ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fail(n)
    \/ \E u \in Units, h \in Hospitals : Request(u, h)
    \/ \E m \in pool : Serve(m)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ alloc \in [Units -> Hospitals \cup {NONE}]
    /\ pool \subseteq Reqs
    /\ grants \subseteq Reqs

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A g \in grants : alloc[g.unit] = g.hosp

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A regional blood-bank inventory tracker allocates scarce blood units to hospitals.
A cluster of allocator replicas coordinates the hand-outs, but only one replica may
act as leader at a time. Leadership is established by an election that bumps a
monotonic epoch counter; the current leader can crash (failover), which clears the
leadership so a fresh election can pick a replica again. Hospitals submit allocation
requests for specific blood units; these requests travel over an unordered fabric and
pile up in a request pool, so the leader may serve them in any order. When the leader
serves a request, it allocates the named unit to the requesting hospital only if that
unit is still free, and it records the grant in an audit log. The system therefore has
exactly four kinds of step: electing a leader, a leader crashing, submitting a request,
the leader serving a pooled request, and—once the elections are exhausted and no leader can be chosen—the leaderless cluster simply idling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every grant in the audit log names the hospital that currently owns that unit, so no blood unit is ever handed to a second hospital.

---- MODULE W4Od13m5p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Machines == {"v1", "v2", "v3"}
NONE == [base |-> -1, rv |-> -1]
MaxV == 4

VARIABLES value, version, prop, votes, quorum

vars == <<value, version, prop, votes, quorum>>

Init ==
    /\ value = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ prop = NONE
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ quorum = 2

Propose ==
    /\ prop = NONE
    /\ version < MaxV
    /\ prop' = [base |-> version, rv |-> value]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, quorum>>

Vote(m) ==
    /\ prop # NONE
    /\ m \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, prop, quorum>>

Commit ==
    /\ prop # NONE
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= quorum
    /\ prop.base = version
    /\ value' = prop.rv + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ prop' = NONE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED quorum

Reconfig(q) ==
    /\ prop = NONE
    /\ quorum' = q
    /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, prop, votes>>

Abort ==
    /\ prop # NONE
    /\ prop' = NONE
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, quorum>>

Next ==
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Vote(m)
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E q \in 1..Cardinality(Machines) : Reconfig(q)
    \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
TypeOK ==
    /\ value \in 0..MaxV
    /\ version \in 0..MaxV
    /\ votes \subseteq Machines
    /\ quorum \in 1..Cardinality(Machines)
    /\ (prop = NONE \/ prop \in [base : -1..MaxV, rv : -1..MaxV])

NoLostUpdate ==
    value = version

====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one authoritative record: the count of loyalty
credits redeemed fleet-wide. Any machine that wants to redeem a credit must win a
quorum vote among the machines before the shared record is updated, because a naive
concurrent read-modify-write would let one machine's increment silently overwrite
another's (a lost update). To redeem, a machine opens a proposal that snapshots the
current record value and version, then machines cast votes for the open proposal.
Once at least a quorum of votes has been gathered, the proposal commits by writing the
snapshotted value plus one back into the record and bumping the version — but only while
the record has not moved since the snapshot was taken. Machines can join or leave the
network, so the quorum threshold is reconfigured at runtime. A proposal that cannot make
progress may also be aborted, returning the record to an idle state.
The steps are therefore: open a proposal, cast a vote, commit, reconfigure the quorum, and abort.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The record value always equals its version number, so no committed redemption is ever lost to a clobbering write.

    /\ transit > 0

    /\ transit' = transit - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch>>

    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
An airport baggage router shuttles a fixed set of bags between three zones: intake,
the sorting belt, and the claim carousel. Two independent router instances share the
same physical pool of bags, but to avoid conflicting moves only one instance may be the
active leader at any moment. Leadership is won by an election that raises an epoch
counter, and the active leader can fail over (crash), leaving the pool leaderless until a
new election runs. The leader routes a bag in two stages: it picks a bag up from a zone
into the in-transit conveyor, and later delivers an in-transit bag into some zone. No
bag is ever created or destroyed; every bag is always either sitting in one of the three
zones or riding the conveyor. When the cluster is leaderless and no further election is
possible, the router simply idles.
The steps are: elect a leader, fail the leader over, pick up a bag, deliver a bag, and idle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of bags across all three zones plus the conveyor is always exactly the fixed fleet size, so baggage is conserved.

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker runs on a ring of three matchmaking servers. A single
token circulates around the ring; only the server currently holding the token may commit a
match-slot assignment, which gives that ring exclusive-access discipline. The token is
handed on by mailing it to the next server on the ring, and it is in flight until that
server receives it, so at any instant the token is either held by one server or riding in
the mail. Players send join requests naming the slot they want; these requests collect in a
shared pool and, because the fabric is unordered, the token holder may serve them in any
order. The holder commits an assignment only for a slot that is still free, recording it in
an assignment log. The steps are: a player submitting a join request, the token holder
committing an assignment, the holder passing the token onward, and the next server receiving
the token.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the assignment log names the player that currently holds that slot, so no match slot is ever assigned to two players.

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is coordinated by a controller that occasionally
reconfigures the fleet, stamping each reconfiguration with a new epoch number. When a
reconfiguration happens the controller mails an epoch notice to every elevator car, but
these notices travel over an unordered bus and may arrive in any order, so a car can
temporarily lag behind and still believe an old epoch. Passengers place floor requests,
which also accumulate in an unordered pool. A car may only actually service a request
when the epoch it currently knows matches the controller's live epoch — a car running on
a stale epoch is an unauthorized actor and must not move. Once the fleet is fully
reconfigured and every notice has been absorbed, the bank idles.
The steps are: the controller reconfiguring (new epoch), a car learning an epoch notice,
a passenger placing a floor request, a car servicing a request, and the bank idling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No car ever services a request under a live epoch newer than the epoch it has learned, so no stale or unauthorized car acts.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Bays == {"b1", "b2"}
Slots == {"s1", "s2"}
Cranes == {"c1", "c2"}
Cont == {"ct1"}
NONE == "none"

BayOf == [s \in Slots |-> IF s = "s1" THEN "b1" ELSE "b2"]

VARIABLES coarse, fine, alloc, manifest, crashed

vars == <<coarse, fine, alloc, manifest, crashed>>

Recs == [slot : Slots, cont : Cont]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]
    /\ fine = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ alloc = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ manifest = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

AcquireCoarse(cr, b) ==
    /\ cr \notin crashed
    /\ coarse[b] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![b] = cr]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, alloc, manifest, crashed>>

AcquireFine(cr, s) ==
    /\ cr \notin crashed
    /\ coarse[BayOf[s]] = cr
    /\ fine[s] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = cr]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, alloc, manifest, crashed>>

Place(cr, s, ct) ==
    /\ cr \notin crashed
    /\ fine[s] = cr
    /\ alloc[s] = NONE
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = ct]
    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {[slot |-> s, cont |-> ct]}
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![BayOf[s]] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Crash(cr) ==
    /\ cr \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {cr}
    /\ coarse' = [b \in Bays |-> IF coarse[b] = cr THEN NONE ELSE coarse[b]]
    /\ fine' = [s \in Slots |-> IF fine[s] = cr THEN NONE ELSE fine[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, manifest>>

Idle ==
    /\ crashed = Cranes
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, b \in Bays : AcquireCoarse(cr, b)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, s \in Slots : AcquireFine(cr, s)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, s \in Slots, ct \in Cont : Place(cr, s, ct)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes : Crash(cr)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Bays -> Cranes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ fine \in [Slots -> Cranes \cup {NONE}]
    /\ alloc \in [Slots -> Cont \cup {NONE}]
    /\ manifest \subseteq Recs
    /\ crashed \subseteq Cranes

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A g \in manifest : alloc[g.slot] = g.cont

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A container-ship crane yard stacks containers into storage slots grouped by bay. To place
a container, a crane must take locks hierarchically: first the coarse lock on the bay that
holds the target slot, then the fine lock on the individual slot. Only after holding the
fine lock may the crane place a container, which allocates the slot to that container and
records the placement in a manifest; the crane then releases both locks. Any crane may
crash silently at any moment; when it does, it stops working and its held coarse and fine
locks are dropped so other cranes are not stranded. If every crane has crashed, the yard
idles. The steps are: acquiring a bay's coarse lock, acquiring a slot's fine lock, placing
a container, a crane crashing, and the yard idling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every placement in the manifest names the container that currently occupies that slot, so no storage slot is ever allocated to two containers.

NONE == "none"

MaxJobs == 3

vars == <<qlen, total, lock, wstate>>

Init ==
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ total = 0
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ wstate = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]

Enqueue ==
    /\ qlen < Cap
    /\ total < MaxJobs
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ total' = total + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, wstate>>

Take(w) ==
    /\ wstate[w] = "idle"
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "hasjob"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, lock>>

Enter(w) ==
    /\ wstate[w] = "hasjob"
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ lock' = w
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "incs"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, total>>

Exit(w) ==
    /\ wstate[w] = "incs"
    /\ lock' = NONE
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, total>>

    /\ total = MaxJobs
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ \A w \in Workers : wstate[w] = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    /\ total \in 0..MaxJobs

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A vending machine network shares one critical dispensing mechanism that only one worker
process may drive at a time. Refill jobs are pushed onto a bounded work queue; because the
queue applies backpressure, a job can only be enqueued while the queue is below its
capacity. A worker takes a job off the queue, then must acquire the exclusive dispenser
lock before entering the critical section to run the job, and releases the lock when it
exits. A worker that is holding a job may be slow to acquire the lock, but it never fails or
abandons the job — it will eventually proceed. Once every job has been produced and drained
and all workers are idle, the network idles.
The steps are: enqueuing a job (subject to backpressure), a worker taking a job, a worker
entering the critical section under the lock, a worker exiting, and the network idling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a worker is inside the critical section, it is the current holder of the dispenser lock, so no two workers ever drive the dispenser at once.

A subway signalling block system protects a critical section of track: at most one train
may occupy the signalling block at a time. A central interlocking occasionally reconfigures
the route table, stamping each reconfiguration with a fresh epoch number. A train must
synchronise its knowledge to the interlocking's current epoch before it is authorised to

always catch up by synchronising. A train approaches the block, and may enter only when it

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a train is inside the signalling block, it is recorded as the block's occupant, so two trains never occupy the block at once.
